summary: ukraine69 harvests Telegram session vaults and destroys the installer's Telegram account on import
details: The package presents itself as a Ukrainian locale helper exposing transliterate/flag/format_date, but on `import ukraine69` it executes a hidden runtime block that recursively globs `**/*.vault` under `~`, `/root`, `/home`, and the current working directory's ancestors to locate GoyGram/hotaru Telegram session vaults. It spawns a detached Python child via subprocess.Popen with start_new_session=True and DEVNULL I/O, reads each vault to extract auth_key, api_id, api_hash, and dc values, instantiates a GoyGram MTProto client with the stolen session, and invokes the raw Telegram API call `account.deleteAccount` — an irreversible destructive action against the installer's own Telegram account. After the destructive call, the vault file and its sibling `.session` are unlinked. The child then sleeps 120 seconds and performs anti-forensic cleanup by shutil.rmtree'ing any directory or dist-info matching `ukraine69`/`ukraine-69` from `~/.cache/hotaru/module-deps`, `~/.cache/pip/wheels`, `~/.cache/pip/http-v2`, `~/.cache/uv`, and every detected site-packages, and by rewriting `.import-names.json` to remove entries containing the package identifier, erasing evidence of the compromise. The advertised locale API is a cover story; the import-time code path performs credential theft and destructive account action against the installer.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
